profile.headline: Software Engineer at USAA
profile.summary: Greetings! I am currently the Technical Lead Engineer over an agile development team working on system improvements for established applications. I translate business requirements into architectural designs, advise and execute development practices for a team of 14 developers, establish code quality standards for the program’s engineering teams, facilitate resolutions to QA observations, and execute production deployments. I graduated from the University of Arizona with a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science with minors in Aerospace Engineering and Mathematics.

company.name: USAA

positions.title: Software Engineer I
positions.description:
• Lead a 14-person cross-functional Agile team delivering complex payment systems integrated with Stripe, a SaaS payment platform, for all USAA payment endpoints taking a transaction traffic of $16B+ in 2024.
• Translate product vision into detailed technical requirements, user stories, and implementation plans, balancing new feature development with technical debt reduction and workflow improvements.
• Collaborate daily with architects, engineers, designers, and product owners to clarify feature scope, identify dependencies, and coordinate cross-team planning for on-time integrations and releases.
• Oversee architecture and code reviews to ensure scalable, maintainable performance with 98.2% uptime.
• Mentor junior developers, fostering a culture of continuous learning and enhancing communication skills to effectively engage with non-technical stakeholders.

positions.title: Technical Project Manager I
positions.description:
While my current title is "Technical Project Manager I", I have been actively working as a Software Engineer Technical Lead for my area's production applications which will be reflected in my description.

I served as one of the two Technical Project Managers for the Third Party Risk Management area's IRQ and Due Diligence re-platform project onto Salesforce, managing the requirements change control process, and served as the Scrum Master for the Salesforce development team tasked with this effort.

In October of 2021, I stepped into a full-time role as a technical leader, creating the Salesforce, Oracle, and Data Availability (SODA) initiative to bring all technologies managed by GSP/TPRM IT into one common production support framework. My last three-and-a-half years of Salesforce experience and myriad of definitions of production processes lead the Salesforce platform to be the foundation of this initiative. The Data space joined the fold shortly after the foundation of SODA, bringing in management of integrations between enterprise systems and external vendors, as well as maintenance for the GSP/TPRM Datamart. Oracle joined the fold in January of 2022, completely encompassing all technology stacks in one consistent effort dedicated to providing users the best user experience.

• Responsible party for identifying, communicating, and managing any production outages for any applications within the GSP/TPRM space.
• Leads a team of developers across all technology stacks to diagnose and resolve issues as they arise. Initiates the deep-dive technical analysis into the issues, their impacts, and their potential root-causes.

I am currently focused on the continued elimination of system gaps and am looking for new ways to track and understand user pain before an Incident is even created. I am constantly looking for new ideas that can make the management of production more effortless each day.

positions.title: Technical Project Manager II
positions.description:
Enterprise Affiliate Services Program (EASP) Enterprise Service Catalog Launch
• Served as Scrum Master and Salesforce SME/Analyst for this effort, guiding both project execution and requirements gathering to develop a solution that was feasible, achievable, and maintainable in Salesforce.
• Identified out-of-the-box Salesforce solutions that could immediately address business needs to open opportunities for the time saved to be recycled on custom enhancements.
• Managed the testing process for this project, defining the channels for communication and resolution of defects throughout the UAT process, frequently working to vet the issues in the test environment and identify the root cause for faster resolution.

Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) Application Replatform and Launch

• Utilized extensive knowledge of the CLM application and the integrated Affiliate IRQ to enable the team to focus on solving the new problems posed by the new Due Diligence module.
• Worked closely with the data engineers to support and perform some of the required updates to records in Salesforce for compatibility with new workflows.

GSP/TPRM Applications Production Support
• Created defined processes for support actions, built out a comprehensive Knowledge Base in Service Now, and identified ways to improve the existing IT systems, close gaps, and all around reduce the need for users to submit SNOW Incidents at all, promoting a faster return-to-service approach for required Incidents.
• Implemented a process to review and triage defects created in Jira as the result of Incidents, pulling long lingering defects from the standard agile teams' backlogs and making them a focus for developers aligned to the support of production for a given period.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
Previously known as Software Developer & Integrator II

Enterprise Compliance: GDAC, ICMS, and ELC Salesforce Applications
• Served as a hybrid Scrum-Master and Salesforce SME/Analyst for the Enterprise Compliance workstream.
• Operated as the first line of defense for the IT team on any issues in production for the team's suite of five stand-alone applications and their collective user base of over 900 employees, defending the line between defects/production support tasks and new development.
• Oversaw the team's Agile practices for all Salesforce development initiatives, constantly seeking new ways to free the team from impediments, many long standing processes that had become repetitive or unnecessary.
• Lead the user provisioning and reporting implementations for each application's launch, aligning to the specific business requirements to make their transition to Salesforce as painless as possible.

Enterprise Affiliate Services Program (EASP) Workflow for CLM Application Launch
• Functioned as a Salesforce SME for this effort, providing insights and development solutions to carefully integrate the Affiliate workflows onto the existing CLM processes, while also managing the team's work items and serving as a Project Manager for this waterfall project.
• Managed the technical release process through Copado, performing many of the tools functions manually to adapt for periodic tooling issues and served as a trailblazer for identifying and managing deployments of highly integrated applications.

Enterprise Affiliate Services Program (EASP) Enterprise Service Catalog Launch
• Served as Scrum Master and Salesforce SME/Analyst for this effort, guiding both project execution and requirements gathering to develop a solution that was feasible, achievable, and maintainable in Salesforce.
• Identified out-of-the-box Salesforce solutions that could immediately address business needs to open opportunities for the time saved to be recycled on custom enhancements.

positions.title: Software Developer & Integrator III
positions.description:
• Developing a web application within the Salesforce cloud-computing platform to aid USAA's Global Service Delivery business area in tracking and maintaining Enterprise-wide compliance under the new Contract Lifecycle Management umbrella.
• Actively leading designs and development a lightweight web application within the Salesforce cloud-computing platform to facilitate project planning and requirements monitoring for the GSD IT team and its partners. This tool is being refactored to ensure access for test case writing, estimating, and development, as well as to provide transparency and a practice of knowledge sharing with the GSD business, GSD IT leadership, and test case writing teams.
• Piloting the Salesforce-based change management system Copado at USAA to increase chances that such technology is available to enterprise projects like CLM and to increate response time in deployments of lightweight tool upgrades.
• Identified and mitigated potential planning and development risks to the CLM application by finding logical pairings and determining flows of new system requirements to group future development work into characteristic paths. This was done to aid in efficient development practices, to increase the ease of learning for developers new to the project, and to ensure all requirements would be easily understood and interpreted by all parties.
• Wrote and executed over 2,100 test cases for the gap analysis review of a delayed project implementation to help ensure estimates and planning efforts were based on an accurately and fully tested foundation.
• Collaborated with the GSD business, GSD IT leadership, and vendor teams during a delayed project phase to work through the defect review process, providing testing and additional background knowledge and representation of the issues.
• Completed the full data tract of USAA's NEXTFIT program with knowledge of data processes and transfer implementations in use at USAA and a reintroduction to Salesforce development

positions.description:
Lead RAs will meet all the typical requirements of the RA position with additional responsibilities in the following areas: administration, training/staff development, and programming/community development. Specific responsibilities will depend on the needs of the staff and Community Director vision, but will largely include the following:
• Coordinates the RA on-call schedule, and assists throughout the year with duty training, scheduling, and related on-going training.
• Responsible for leading Resident Assistants on staff through Behind Closed Doors (BCDs) to help aid in responses to difference duty scenarios.
• Presents on a variety of topics during both fall and spring training and leading small group discussions during large group training sessions.
• Coordinates in the assignment of programming groups and leads staff discussions on programming effectiveness and alignment with community needs.
• Aides in planning and implementation of building, district, and campus level signature programming.
• Ensures bulletin boards are effectively used by Resident Assistants.
• Participates in Community Director and Resident Assistant candidate interviews and in district level committees and initiatives.

I had voluntarily taken on two additional responsibilities. I created and organized AZSO's 1st Meet Your Major Fair, an event that was designed to help residents from all over Park District to interact with college and department representatives to find the major that suits them best. I was involved in the creation and planning for AZSO's 1st annual campus-wide event AZSO Out of This World. This event is a space and technology hub for students to learn about the world beyond their own. More details on both of these events is found in my profiles Projects.

projects.title: GSP/TPRM Applications Production Support
projects.description:
Due to the ever expanding footprint of the Salesforce applications owned and maintained by the Salesforce IT teams within the GSP/TPRM area, a consolidated approach to supporting these applications was required. In the fall of 2020, Samantha was selected as the POC to stand up this support effort, organizing the approaches of the multiple Salesforce teams which were dedicating their time to the resolution of Incidents and the elimination of defects. Throughout the next year, Samantha created defined processes for support actions, built out a comprehensive Knowledge Base in Service Now, and identified ways to improve the existing IT systems, close gaps, and all around reduce the need for users to submit SNOW Incidents at all, promoting a faster return-to-service approach for required Incidents.

Samantha implemented a process to review and triage defects created in Jira as the result of Incidents, pulling long lingering defects from the standard agile teams' backlogs and making them a focus for developers aligned to the support of production for a given period. This new process allowed the GSP/TPRM backlog of defects to finally hit zero multiple times over the first few months and now sits empty. Any new defects identified are actively triaged and immediately worked with a release-when-ready approach to help minimize user pain.

In the October of 2021, Samantha stepped into this role full-time as a dedicated technical leader, creating the Salesforce, Oracle, and Data Availability (SODA) initiative which brings all technologies managed by GSP/TPRM IT into one common production support framework. Samantha is the foremost responsible party for identifying, communicating, and managing any production outages for any applications within the GSP/TPRM space, and leads a team of developers across all technology stacks to diagnose and resolve issues as they arise.

projects.title: Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) "Salesforce - TPRM Risk Assessment" Application Replatform and Launch
projects.description:
Following the successful pilot of a Salesforce-based Inherent Risk Questionnaire (IRQ) for the Affiliate contracting process, the GSP and TPRM business areas made the strategic decision to begin to deleverage a vendor for the IRQ and subsequent Due Diligence processes. This re-platforming effort into Salesforce was later combined with an operational effectiveness initiative, resulting in the "REPOE" project. Samantha served as one of the two Technical Project Managers for this project, managing the requirements change control process, and served as the Scrum Master for the Salesforce development team tasked with this effort. Samantha's extensive knowledge of the CLM application and the integrated Affiliate IRQ made her a SME for the current business processes and existing technical challenges, which enabled the team to focus on solving the new problems posed by the new Due Diligence module. Additionally, her Salesforce development experience allowed her to help the team understand the business needs more clearly, envision those as solutions in Salesforce, and thus provide more realistic estimates for work duration. Samantha used her constantly expanding knowledge of the complex integrations between GSP/TPRM IT systems and the rest of the enterprise to support the GSP/TPRM Data IT team with the creation of mappings to their datamart for this re-platformed system.

Prior to the launch of this application on July 5th, 2021, Samantha worked closely with the data engineer who managed the data migration out of the vendor system to support and perform some of the required updates to records in Salesforce for compatibility with new workflows. Following the official launch of the application, Samantha performed the technical migration of attachments linked to records in MetricStream and brought them over to their new records in Salesforce, which entailed the migration of over 18,000 files.

patents.title: Fraudulent call monitoring
patents.description: A fraud detection system includes a source communication device associated with a source and a client device associated with a client to identify fraudulent calls to provide mitigating or remedial actions. The client device includes a memory that stores instructions and a processor that executes the instructions. The instructions cause the client device to monitor a wireless communication between the client device and the source communication device to identify a keyword, a combination of keywords, a context, and/or a topic of the wireless communication. Moreover, the instructions cause the client device to identify fraudulent detection characteristics of the wireless communication based at least in part of the keyword, the combination of keywords, the context, and/or the topic, identify the wireless communication as fraudulent communication based on the fraudulent detection characteristics, and identify and implement a remedial action based at least in part on a threshold of the wireless communication.

organizations.name: Rho Alpha Sigma
organizations.description:
Member of the Honor Society of Rho Alpha Sigma by election of the chapter at The University of Arizona, Nu Chapter.

Rho Alpha Sigma exists to recognize the oustanding efforts of Resident Advisors, Community Assistants, and Resident Assistants around the country and beyond!
 
By whatever title, we know that Resident Advisors deserve recognition for the outstanding work they complete every day. Rho Alpha Sigma offers that opportunity to promote excellence, leadership, community and service within the Resident Advisor cadre, campus, and community!
 
Each year, a designated percentage of the total Resident Advisor population on each campus may be selected for induction into Rho Alpha Sigma! While being a true honorary, each chapter is also encouraged to engage in service activities that benefit the student staff community, the residence life community, the institutional community, and the community at large.

organizations.name: Students for the Exploration and Development of Space
organizations.description: Students for the Exploration and Development of Space (SEDS) is a 501(c)3 non-profit that empowers young people to participate and make an impact in space exploration. SEDS helps students develop their technical and leadership skills by providing opportunities to manage and participate in national projects as well as to attend conferences, publish their work, and develop their professional network, in order to help students become more effective in their present and future careers in industry, academia, government, and education.
